To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a large glycoprotein, containing two major subunit species, has been identified as the acceptor for dendrotoxins in bovine synaptic plasma membrane.

dendrotoxin is an extremely potent and selective blocker of voltage-activated K+-channels and that the acceptor for this toxin is a large oligomerc glycoprotein, with a subunit structure of 2 X 37,000 and 75,000.

a novel, large, glycosylated oligomeric protein from bovine brain, containing two major subunit species of 75, and 37 kDa, binds dendrotoxin with a dissociation constant of 1.3 nM and is a constituent of certain voltage-sensitive, K+ channels in brain membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the purification and characterization of the acceptor protein from synaptic plasma membranes for dendrotoxins, a family of snake polypeptides which selectively and potently inhibit certain voltage-dependent potassium channels.
the identification of K+-channel constituents in the nervous system.
the identification of the dendrotoxin acceptors and with their possible involvement in the function of certain voltage-sensitive, K+ channels in mammalian nerve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dendrotoxin binds to a glycoprotein acceptor, with Mr values between 75,000-90,000, which is composed of two subunits of 37,000 and 75,000, and which is a constituent of a voltage-activated K+-channel in the central nervous system.

the dendrotoxin receptor in bovine synaptic plasma membrane is a glycoprotein with an Mr of 120,000-130,000 and a subunit composition of alpha 1 (75,000) and alpha 2 (37,000), which is the same subunit composition as the K+-channel protein purified from bovine adrenal medulla.
the purified protein is the acceptor for dendrotoxins and, hence, the putative constituent of a certain type of voltage-activated K+-channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acceptor protein from bovine synapses, a putative K+- channel subunit, is a glycoprotein of Mr 112,000 that contains two polypeptides of Mr 75,000 (A-subunit) and 37, 000 (B-subunit).
the dendrotoxin acceptors from bovine brain are large, oligomeric, membrane-bound glycoproteins with two subunits, Mr 75,000 (alpha) and 37, 000 (beta).
the acceptor is an oligomeric glycolipoprotein with subunit Mr values of 37,000 and 75,000.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acceptor protein has a high affinity for dendrotoxins, but it does not bind to the other toxins studied.
dendrotoxin acceptors in brain membranes appear to be composed of two major subunits with apparent molecular masses of 75, 000 and 37.000.

the dendrotoxin acceptors in the bovine brain and the venom glands of the green mamba snake (Dendroaspis angusticeps) are structurally and functionally related proteins, which may be the same or similar to the acceptors for dendrotoxins in other snake venoms and in other tissues.
